text.H1: How long should an autopilot flight take?
text.LEDE: Eight flights by the new autopilot, each at three settings side by side. They play at game speed, from the click until the ship is in orbit. A two-sun flight can change by up to 13 s with the moment you click, so the line under each flight gives the range over ten clicks a tenth of a second apart.
text.PICKS: Reply with a letter: Flight length: A, B or C
text.A_STAT: ONE SUN, PLACE TO PLACE: MEDIAN 23.5 S, LONGEST 30.6 S
text.A_TEXT: Place to place, flights of about 24 s, nine in ten under 30 s. The first flight after a jump takes about 29 s. Built and tested; nothing more to write before the branch lands.
text.B_STAT: ONE SUN, PLACE TO PLACE: MEDIAN 18.9 S, LONGEST 23.7 S
text.B_TEXT: Place to place, flights of about 19 s, nine in ten under 23 s: the pace you picked on the Orbits v2 page. The first flight after a jump takes about 23 s. Needs about 100 lines of new solver code with tests, and one failing test fixed.
text.C_STAT: ONE SUN, PLACE TO PLACE: MEDIAN 10.8 S, LONGEST 20.0 S
text.C_TEXT: Place to place, flights of about 11 s, nine in ten under 15 s. The first flight after a jump takes about 18 s. The engine burns about three times as long as A's. Needs the same new code as B, and one failing test fixed.
text.AFTER: At every setting, a two-sun flight that needs two legs takes about 48 s, up to 57. About 1 twin flight in 85 needs two legs. Flying inside a system costs no fuel at any setting.
text.TODAY: Today's autopilot on the four one-sun flights, from the same clicks. Over every one-sun flight between places it took 6.9 s median and 12.1 s at most. It cannot fly to the second sun, so it has no two-sun flights.
text.HOW:
• Measured headless, one Godot at a time, on feat/twin-fix (ee5ef1d3) with B's and C's changes added as study code. One second of map time is one second on the wall.
  • The medians and longest times are from FlightTest's full runs, from the click to settled in orbit, for flights between places in one-sun systems. Over all 1,478 game starts in twins the medians are A 24.4 s, B 21.5 s and C 14.0 s.
  • From an orbit of the sun or just after a jump, B and C sometimes fall back to A's search, so their longest one-sun flights from any start are A 30.6 s, B 29.9 s and C 27.3 s. With a heavy giant they are 39.5, 36.4 and 34.4 s.
  • B lands later than A from about 1 start in 13, by up to 13 s. In twins about 1 start in 33 is later by over 5 s. C lands later from about 1 start in 55, by up to 6 s. Where B is later, it mostly picked a flight that works its engine less.
  • Before B or C can land: B fails one SolveTest replan check, and C fails one SolveTest check where a burn slows to a cusp (1 of 2,610 twin flights). C also leaves one test-only start grazing a keep-out.
  • No setting loses a flight A finds. SolveTest's 12,648 plans were compared case by case.
  • Each replay is the one of its ten clicks nearest that setting's median.
  • Drawn as the map draws them, at the zoom it opens at, in game pixels doubled: the ship's arrow (not your hull's picture), its trail, its plan line, its rings and the reticles. Names and labels are left out.
  • Settings: A is TIME_W 0.5, T_CAP 30. B is TIME_W 1, T_CAP 23. C is TIME_W 16, T_CAP 16.
